changes.old: Magnesium glycinate is one of the more approachable gifts in this whole guide, because it doesn't ask the recipient to change anything about their evening routine — it's just something they take before bed instead of another supplement. It's a particularly fitting gift for anyone working rotating shifts or irregular hours, since it's one of the lower-risk, better-tolerated options some shift workers add alongside light management and a consistent wind-down routine, rather than a replacement for either. changes.old: Weighted blankets have graduated from trend to staple, and for good reason — they're one of the few sleep-wellness products people keep using years after buying, rather than abandoning after a month. The idea behind them is deep pressure stimulation, a gentle, even pressure some research links to reduced physiological arousal and modest improvements in self-reported sleep quality and anxiety symptoms, though the evidence isn't universal and isn't a substitute for treating a diagnosed sleep or anxiety disorder. Sizing matters more than most gift-givers expect — the general guideline is a blanket roughly 10% of the recipient's body weight, so if you're unsure of their exact weight, it's worth checking with someone close to them or leaning toward a mid-range weight and letting them exchange it. It's also not the right gift for a notoriously hot sleeper unless you specifically choose a cooling-weave version, or for young children and anyone with certain respiratory or circulatory conditions without medical guidance. Our full breakdown on {{ '/posts/weighted-blankets-sleep-anxiety/' | url }} covers weight charts, material differences, and who this helps most.
